text:
alex: Heads-up — noticed a reproducible window where a tenant's prefix is demoted and then immediately rehydrated on another node, but the eviction token checklets still think the old owner is valid. logs: `evict: lease_e=42 != lease_o=41` :confused:
mina: ugh, seen something similar in canary last week. do you have a small repro? :eyes:
alex: yeah I have a short repro harness that triggers when demote+handback happen within ~50ms. attaching snippet:
alex: ```
# simplified repro loop
claim_prefix(pfx)
demote_prefix(pfx)
handback_prefix(pfx)
read_with_prefetch(pfx)
```
ryan: what's the invariance we expect? that an ownership token is always strictly monotonic (epoch, seq)? or is there a plausible transient where two nodes both think they own it?
jessie: we currently rely on a soft-lease id + best-effort demote; there is a tiny race where demote is acknowledged but the token isn't fully propagated to the eviction scorer. scorer then skips eviction because it sees a matching lease id in cache metadata.
mina: proposal: change the ownership token to a 3-tuple (epoch, owner_id, commit_seq) and make eviction require commit_seq >= seen_seq. that way a stale owner loses rights even if epoch matches. downside is more metadata and need to carry commit_seq on handoff RPCs.
ryan: another option: introduce a two-phase demote where demote returns a "grace-cutoff" ts that eviction uses to accept demotes immediately and reject any older commits. simpler but brittle with clock skew.
alex: I prefer the (epoch, seq) approach — deterministic and no clock dependence. also we can piggyback seq on existing handshake RPCs so perf hit is minimal.
jessie: agree on deterministic. we should also add an acceptance test that flips nodes rapidly and asserts there are no double-owns for the same prefix for >1ms.
prefetch-bot: metric alert: prefix_handoff_retries increased 8x in canary at 2026-03-17T14:10Z :warning:
mina: ok action items: (1) I'll draft a short RFC describing the (epoch,owner,seq) token and eviction contract, (2) Ryan + Alex will implement scorer check and handshake changes, (3) Jessie will add canary + replay test harness. I'll put owners in the RFC.
ryan: one more tradeoff to call out — making seq mandatory means older snapshots without seq are treated as seq=0 and could be demoted unexpectedly on upgrade. need an upgrade plan: tolerate missing seq by treating them as always older and require a coordinated roll-out or a compatibility flag.
alex: noted. RFC should include compatibility plan and a small transition API: `handshake({owner,epoch,seq||null})` and scorer treats null as -inf until we flip the flag.
mina: timeline? can we aim RFC + tests this sprint and a canary rollout next?
jessie: yes. I'll carve out time for the harness. also will add a `--chaos-fast-handoff` option to the harness so we can stress the race.
alex: thanks. i'll upload the repro files to the RFC PR. :thumbsup:
mina: thanks all — i'll create the RFC and tag you. keeping this thread for coordination.
ryan: :+1:
jessie: :rocket:
